-- ── NUM_CHAT_WINDOWS — how many chat windows the UI declares ───────────────────────── -- `NUM_CHAT_WINDOWS = 7` is ChatFrame.lua line 5, verbatim. It is a FrameXML constant, not -- an engine one, and the number is NOT the engine's: the chat-cache and the per-window -- struct array `0xb4fe50` (wow-re `chat-color-table.md`, stride 0x98) both hold **10** -- windows, and FloatingChatFrame.xml duly declares ChatFrame1TabDockRegion..10 — but only -- seven ChatFrames. 7 is the count an addon iterates. -- -- Measured demand: **5 corpus addons, all genuinely distinct** (no replicated library — -- the one clean count in this area). Two idioms, and they need different things from us: -- getglobal("ChatFrame"..i) Outfitter, _LazyPig — _LazyPig indexes the result -- UNGUARDED (`ChatFrame:IsVisible()`), so it dies at i=3 -- unless ChatFrame3..7 are real frames. They are, below. -- GetChatWindowInfo(i) EnhTooltip, MikScrollingBattleText, Enchantrix — the -- engine getter, `benilla_ui::script::chat_window`. NUM_CHAT_WINDOWS = 7
-- ── SlashCmdList — the addon slash-command registry (decision 1195) ──────────────────── -- Declared HERE, not in Rust, because the 1.12 client declares it in ChatFrame.lua and the -- captured `_G` attributes it `table framexml`. An addon's registration is three lines at -- FILE SCOPE: -- SLASH_MYADDON1 = "/myaddon" -- SlashCmdList["MYADDON"] = function(msg) ... end -- so a missing table is not a missing feature, it is `attempt to index global -- 'SlashCmdList'` on the addon's very first chunk — 26 of a 218-addon corpus died there. -- The dispatch walk is `benilla_ui::script::slash`, transcribing ChatEdit_ParseText's. -- -- It starts EMPTY: benilla's own commands are dispatched host-side (decision 0881's table) -- where the reference registers them here. That divergence is recorded in `slash.rs`. SlashCmdList = {}
-- ── ChatTypeGroup / OtherMenuChatTypeGroups — declared, and deliberately EMPTY ──────── -- The reference builds `ChatTypeGroup` at ChatFrame.lua l.115-348: 68 entries mapping a -- chat TYPE to the list of `CHAT_MSG_*` events that belong to it, which its -- `ChatFrame_RegisterForMessages` walks to register events on a chat window. -- -- Declared here for the same reason `SlashCmdList` above is: an addon REGISTERS ITS OWN -- chat type at file scope, and a missing table is not a missing feature — it is -- `attempt to index global 'ChatTypeGroup'` on the addon's very first chunk. CT_RaidAssist -- does exactly that three lines apart (`CT_RaidAssist.lua:59` assigns -- `ChatTypeGroup["CTRAID"]`, `:63` tinserts into `OtherMenuChatTypeGroups`), and it dies -- there — taking `CT_RA_OnEvent` with it, which is why FOUR MORE corpus addons -- (CT_RABossMods, FixCTGroups, FuBar_CTRaid, SmartRes) die on that function being nil. -- One missing table, five addons. -- -- **EMPTY, not populated, and that is the honest shape rather than a shortcut.** Two -- reasons, in order of weight: -- · The 68 entries are 233 lines of the reference's own Lua. We RUN the reference's -- files where we can (1234) and write our own where we cannot; what we do not do is -- paste its source into a repo that mirrors publicly. -- · Nothing would read them. Measured across the 218-addon corpus with `grep -a`: -- CT_RaidAssist is the ONLY addon that touches either table, and it only WRITES. Not -- one addon reads a group out. -- -- The divergence that leaves, stated rather than discovered: our chat frames do not -- register through this table at all — `ui_chat` routes host-side, the same split -- `SlashCmdList` records above. So an addon that adds a group gets no routing from it. -- That is the `ChatFrame_OnEvent` architecture question, not this table's. ChatTypeGroup = {} OtherMenuChatTypeGroups = {}
-- ── ChatTypeInfo — the per-chat-type table addons read colors out of ────────────────── -- Declared HERE because the 1.12 client declares it at the top of ChatFrame.lua, and it -- is an ADDON-FACING table before it is ours: `local info = ChatTypeInfo["SAY"]` then -- `frame:AddMessage(text, info.r, info.g, info.b, info.id)` is the standard way an addon -- prints a colored line. -- -- Measured, and the raw count is misleading enough to be worth writing down: 234 corpus -- sites, but **192 of them are one line** — AceEvent-2.0's -- `ChatTypeInfo and ChatTypeInfo.WHISPER and ChatTypeInfo.WHISPER.r`, a GUARDED readiness -- probe that copy-pastes into 64 addons and cannot raise. The reads that actually index -- the table are 42 sites in 6 addons (ChatLog, oRA2/Participant's RaidWarn, Glory-2.0's -- two FuBar hosts, FuBar_HeyFu) — those are `attempt to index global 'ChatTypeInfo'` -- without it, and they are the reason this exists. -- -- Three columns, three sources: -- sticky the reference's own literals (ChatFrame.lua l.10-114) — the five sticky types -- are SAY/PARTY/RAID/GUILD/BATTLEGROUND, which `ui_chat::edit` already quotes. -- id GetChatTypeIndex's 1-based index into the engine's 94-entry color registry -- (wow-re `chat-color-table.md`, static table 0x804710) — the ref sets it in -- ChatFrame_OnLoad, and AddMessage's 5th argument is what consumes it. -- r,g,b that registry's byte defaults, /255 — the engine hands Lua 0..1 floats -- (it re-normalizes with the f32 1/255 at 0x8026c8). -- -- ONE DIVERGENCE, and it is a shortcut through a two-step: the reference's OnLoad writes -- 1.0/1.0/1.0 into every entry and waits for the engine's UPDATE_CHAT_COLOR storm to fill -- the real values in (ChatFrame.lua l.1349 is the only writer in the whole default UI). -- benilla has no chat-color settings surface and nothing that fires that event, so the -- values are seeded at their END STATE directly. `ui_chat::event::default_color` is the -- same wow-re table rendered host-side for our own feed, and -- `chat_type_info_matches_the_host_color_table` fails if the two ever drift. -- -- REPLY and COMBAT_ERROR are the two keys FrameXML declares that the engine's registry -- does NOT contain, so GetChatTypeIndex answers 0 for both and no UPDATE_CHAT_COLOR is -- ever fired for either name. They do NOT share a fate, and the first version of this -- block got that wrong by generalising: -- COMBAT_ERROR nothing writes it, ever — id 0, white, on the real client too. -- REPLY the UPDATE_CHAT_COLOR handler MIRRORS WHISPER INTO IT by hand -- (ChatFrame.lua l.1357-1365: `if strupper(arg1) == "WHISPER" then -- info = ChatTypeInfo["REPLY"] ... end`). So its end state is WHISPER's -- FF80FF, which is what the /r header shows, and seeding it white was a -- bug the comment above it was busy justifying. -- CHANNEL1..CHANNEL10 are the boot-seeded extras (indices 95-104), each colored from the -- live CHANNEL entry — FFC0C0. -- ── BenillaFCF: the FloatingChatFrame behaviors, re-expressed (ref FloatingChatFrame.lua) -- Quoted constants: CHAT_TAB_SHOW_DELAY=0.2, CHAT_FRAME_FADE_TIME=0.15, -- DEFAULT_CHATFRAME_ALPHA=0.25, CHAT_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME=0.5, -- MESSAGE_SCROLLBUTTON_INITIAL_DELAY=0, MESSAGE_SCROLLBUTTON_SCROLL_DELAY=0.05. BenillaFCF = { selected = 1, -- SELECTED_DOCK_FRAME (1 = General, 2 = Combat Log) hover = false, -- cursor inside the dock's padded rect hoverTime = 0, -- stationary-cursor accumulator (ref: moving resets it) oldX = 0, oldY = 0, reveal = 0, -- 0..1 master fade the tab/texture alphas scale by revealTarget = 0, flashTab = 0, -- tab id whose whisper flash runs (0 = none), 0288 P4 wires it flashLeft = 0, -- remaining flash seconds (ref: 60s, blink 0.25/0.25) }
-- The per-window texture sets the hover fade drives (ref CHAT_FRAME_TEXTURES: the -- background + the 8 border pieces; benilla authors the borders as plain textures — -- resizing is settings, the hover LOOK is not). Global: the load-time tint below needs it. function BenillaFCF_Textures(id) local n = "ChatFrame" .. id local list = {} for _, suffix in ipairs({ "Background", "BorderTopLeft", "BorderTopRight", "BorderBottomLeft", "BorderBottomRight", "BorderTop", "BorderBottom", "BorderLeft", "BorderRight", }) do local t = getglobal(n .. suffix) if t then table.insert(list, t) end end return list end
-- FCF_SelectDockFrame: show the selected frame, hide the other; selected tab full alpha, -- unselected half (both still scaled by the reveal fade below). Stops the selected tab's -- whisper flash (ref FCF_SelectDockFrame → UIFrameFlashRemoveFrame). Tab getglobals are -- guarded: window 2's tab is deliberately unbuilt (see the note at the tab section). function BenillaFCF_SelectDock(id) BenillaFCF.selected = id for i = 1, 2 do local frame = getglobal("ChatFrame" .. i) if i == id then frame:Show() else frame:Hide() end end if BenillaFCF.flashTab == id then BenillaFCF.flashTab = 0 local flash = getglobal("ChatFrame" .. id .. "TabFlash") if flash then flash:Hide() end end end
-- FCF_SelectDockFrame(frame) — the reference's own name for the operation above, taking a -- FRAME where ours takes a dock id. Both corpus callers pass DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME: -- -- if not DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:IsVisible() then -- FCF_SelectDockFrame(DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME) -- end -- DEFAULT_CHAT_FRAME:AddMessage(out) -- -- verbatim in both CustomNameplates (`CustomNameplates.lua:69`) and Roid-Macros -- (`Utility.lua:40`) — "un-hide the chat window before printing into it". Two addons, -- two independent files, not a replicated library. -- -- Ours does the dock half and NOT the rest of ref FCF_SelectDockFrame l.1204-1217: the ref -- also assigns `SELECTED_DOCK_FRAME` (a global no corpus addon reads — 0 hits) and calls -- `FCF_DockUpdate()` (tab geometry, which FCF_OnUpdate below re-derives every frame). -- -- An UNDOCKED frame RAISES rather than quietly doing nothing. ChatFrame3..7 exist as real -- frames but benilla has no undock/dock model at all (0288 §2 — window management is chat -- settings, deliberately out), so "select ChatFrame5" has no meaning here; answering it -- with silence would leave the caller's next AddMessage landing in a window that is still -- hidden, which is the bug the guard was written to prevent. function FCF_SelectDockFrame(frame) if not frame then error("FCF_SelectDockFrame: nil frame", 2) end local id = frame:GetID() if id ~= 1 and id ~= 2 then error("FCF_SelectDockFrame: " .. (frame:GetName() or "?") .. " is not docked — benilla docks only ChatFrame1/ChatFrame2 (decision 0288 §2)", 2) end BenillaFCF_SelectDock(id) end
function BenillaFCF_TabClick(id) -- ref FCF_Tab_OnClick (docked, left click): select; UChatScrollButton per click. BenillaFCF_SelectDock(id) PlaySound("UChatScrollButton") end
-- The whisper tab flash (ref FCF_FlashTab: never the selected tab; 0.25s on/off for 60s, -- and a flashing tab holds the dock tabs visible). Fired by the app on a received -- whisper landing in an unselected window (0288 P4). No-tab windows can't flash. function BenillaFCF_FlashTab(id) if id == BenillaFCF.selected then return end if not getglobal("ChatFrame" .. id .. "TabFlash") then return end BenillaFCF.flashTab = id BenillaFCF.flashLeft = 60 end
-- PanelTemplates_TabResize(5, tab), re-expressed: the ref sizes every docked tab to its -- label (FCF_DockUpdate) — middle slice = text width + 5, tab = middle + the two 16px -- caps; the flash/highlight bands follow the Left/Right pieces by anchor. The label -- width is host-measured (GetStringWidth), so early frames may see 0 — the OnUpdate -- below re-applies until it settles, then the change-guard makes this a no-op. function BenillaFCF_TabResize(tab) local w = getglobal(tab:GetName() .. "Text"):GetStringWidth() if w == 0 or tab.benillaTabTextW == w then return end tab.benillaTabTextW = w getglobal(tab:GetName() .. "Middle"):SetWidth(w + 5) tab:SetWidth(w + 5 + 32) end
-- The hover rect: the dock's rect expanded by the ref's MouseIsOver pads -- (FCF_OnUpdate: MouseIsOver(chatFrame, 45, -10, -5, 5) — 45 up into the tab zone, -- 10 down past the edit box seam, 5 out each side). local function overDock(x, y) local f = ChatFrame1 local left, right = f:GetLeft(), f:GetRight() local top, bottom = f:GetTop(), f:GetBottom() if not left then return false end return x >= left - 5 and x <= right + 5 and y >= bottom - 10 and y <= top + 45 end
-- FCF_OnUpdate transcription (the parts that survive with window management out): -- reveal after a 0.2s STATIONARY hover (a moving cursor keeps resetting the delay), -- fade over 0.15s, conceal on leave; a flashing tab forces the tabs visible; the -- selected window's textures ride the same fade toward alpha 0.25 (the chat-cache -- default window alpha is 0 — the box only exists on hover). function FCF_OnUpdate(elapsed) local s = BenillaFCF local x, y = GetCursorPosition() if overDock(x, y) then if not s.hover then s.hover = true s.hoverTime = 0 s.oldX, s.oldY = x, y elseif s.oldX == x and s.oldY == y then s.hoverTime = s.hoverTime + elapsed else s.hoverTime = 0 s.oldX, s.oldY = x, y end if s.hoverTime > 0.2 then s.revealTarget = 1 end else s.hover = false s.hoverTime = 0 s.revealTarget = 0 end if s.flashTab ~= 0 then s.revealTarget = 1 end
-- The 0.15s linear fade toward the target (ref UIFrameFadeIn/Out over -- CHAT_FRAME_FADE_TIME). if s.reveal < s.revealTarget then s.reveal = math.min(s.revealTarget, s.reveal + elapsed / 0.15) elseif s.reveal > s.revealTarget then s.reveal = math.max(s.revealTarget, s.reveal - elapsed / 0.15) end
-- Apply: tabs at 1.0 (selected) / 0.5 (unselected) × reveal; the selected window's -- background+borders at 0.25 × reveal (ref: fade oldAlpha↔DEFAULT_CHATFRAME_ALPHA). for i = 1, 2 do local tab = getglobal("ChatFrame" .. i .. "Tab") if tab then local a = (i == BenillaFCF.selected) and 1.0 or 0.5 tab:SetAlpha(a * s.reveal) BenillaFCF_TabResize(tab) end for _, t in ipairs(BenillaFCF_Textures(i)) do t:SetAlpha(0.25 * s.reveal) end end
-- The whisper flash blink (0.25 on / 0.25 off, 60s — ref UIFrameFlash args). if s.flashTab ~= 0 then s.flashLeft = s.flashLeft - elapsed local flash = getglobal("ChatFrame" .. s.flashTab .. "TabFlash") if s.flashLeft <= 0 then s.flashTab = 0 flash:Hide() else local phase = mod(s.flashLeft, 0.5) if phase > 0.25 then flash:Show() else flash:Hide() end end end end
-- ChatFrame_OnUpdate transcription: the bottom button's blink while scrolled up -- (CHAT_BUTTON_FLASH_TIME = 0.5s toggle; hidden the moment the view is AtBottom). function ChatFrame_OnUpdate(elapsed) local frame = this local flash = getglobal(frame:GetName() .. "BottomButtonFlash") if not flash then return end if frame:AtBottom() then flash:Hide() frame.flashTimer = 0 return end frame.flashTimer = (frame.flashTimer or 0) + elapsed while frame.flashTimer >= 0.5 do frame.flashTimer = frame.flashTimer - 0.5 if flash:IsVisible() then flash:Hide() else flash:Show() end end end
-- A completed left click on the chat body dismisses a held SPELL/ACTION payload -- (decision 0843, the director's call — no ref counterpart: the reference keeps a -- non-item payload on any frame click). Items are deliberately excluded: an item -- dismissal is a destroy, which only the world-drop popup flow may offer. function BenillaChatFrame_DismissCursor(button) if button ~= "LeftButton" then return end local kind = GetCursorInfo() if kind == "spell" or kind == "action" then ClearCursor() end end
-- MessageFrameScrollButton_OnLoad/_OnUpdate + the ref OnClick pair: a press arms the -- hold-repeat (initial delay 0), each 0.05s while held scrolls WITHOUT the sound; the -- release click scrolls once WITH the sound (ref FloatingChatFrame.xml's DownButton/ -- UpButton scripts — sound only on the non-pushed branch). function BenillaChatScrollButton_OnClick(btn, down, dir, sound) if down then btn.clickDelay = 0 else PlaySound(sound) local frame = getglobal("ChatFrame" .. BenillaFCF.selected) if dir == "up" then frame:ScrollUp() else frame:ScrollDown() end end end
function BenillaChatScrollButton_OnUpdate(btn, elapsed, dir) if btn:GetButtonState() == "PUSHED" then btn.clickDelay = (btn.clickDelay or 0) - elapsed if btn.clickDelay < 0 then local frame = getglobal("ChatFrame" .. BenillaFCF.selected) if dir == "up" then frame:ScrollUp() else frame:ScrollDown() end btn.clickDelay = 0.05 end end end
-- ── BenillaUIMenu: the 1.12 UIMenu kit, re-expressed (ref UIMenu.lua — the chat menu's -- row engine: fixed 16px rows in a tooltip-backdrop box, a 2 s no-hover timeout that -- walks up parentMenu chains, nested submenus opened on row hover). Constants quoted. -- Scoped here because the chat menu is its only consumer; a second consumer graduates -- it to its own file. BENILLA_UIMENU_BUTTON_HEIGHT = 16 BENILLA_UIMENU_BUTTON_WIDTH = 104 BENILLA_UIMENU_BORDER_HEIGHT = 12 BENILLA_UIMENU_BORDER_WIDTH = 12 BENILLA_UIMENU_NUMBUTTONS = 32 BENILLA_UIMENU_TIMEOUT = 2.0
function UIMenu_Initialize() local menu = this menu.numButtons = 0 menu.subMenu = "" local name = menu:GetName() for i = 1, BENILLA_UIMENU_NUMBUTTONS do local button = getglobal(name .. "Button" .. i) button:SetWidth(BENILLA_UIMENU_BUTTON_WIDTH) button:SetHeight(BENILLA_UIMENU_BUTTON_HEIGHT) button:Hide() getglobal(button:GetName() .. "ShortcutText"):Hide() end menu:SetWidth(BENILLA_UIMENU_BUTTON_WIDTH + BENILLA_UIMENU_BORDER_WIDTH * 2) menu:SetHeight(BENILLA_UIMENU_BORDER_HEIGHT * 2) end
-- Rows past the button pool are dropped (the ref message()s; nothing we author overflows). function UIMenu_AddButton(text, shortcut, func, nested) local menu = this local id = menu.numButtons + 1 if id > BENILLA_UIMENU_NUMBUTTONS then return end menu.numButtons = id local button = getglobal(menu:GetName() .. "Button" .. id) if text then button:SetText(text) end button.func = func button.nested = nested button:Show() if shortcut then local s = getglobal(button:GetName() .. "ShortcutText") s:SetText(shortcut) s:Show() end menu:SetHeight(id * BENILLA_UIMENU_BUTTON_HEIGHT + BENILLA_UIMENU_BORDER_HEIGHT * 2) end
function UIMenu_OnShow() this.timeleft = BENILLA_UIMENU_TIMEOUT this.counting = 1 end
function UIMenu_OnUpdate(elapsed) if this.counting == 1 then local timeleft = (this.timeleft or BENILLA_UIMENU_TIMEOUT) - elapsed if timeleft <= 0 then this:Hide() return end this.timeleft = timeleft end end
function UIMenu_StartCounting(menu) menu.counting = 1 if menu.parentMenu then UIMenu_StartCounting(getglobal(menu.parentMenu)) end end
function UIMenu_StopCounting(menu) menu.counting = 0 menu.timeleft = BENILLA_UIMENU_TIMEOUT if menu.parentMenu then UIMenu_StopCounting(getglobal(menu.parentMenu)) end end
function UIMenuButton_OnLoad() this:SetPoint("TOP", this:GetParent():GetName(), "TOP", 0, -((this:GetID() - 1) * BENILLA_UIMENU_BUTTON_HEIGHT) - BENILLA_UIMENU_BORDER_HEIGHT) end
function UIMenuButton_OnClick() if this.func then this.func() end this:GetParent():Hide() PlaySound("UChatScrollButton") end
function UIMenuButton_OnEnter() local nested = this.nested if nested then local menu = getglobal(nested) if not menu:IsVisible() then local oldMenu = getglobal(this:GetParent().subMenu or "") if oldMenu then oldMenu:Hide() end this:GetParent().subMenu = nested menu:SetPoint("BOTTOMLEFT", this:GetName(), "BOTTOMRIGHT", 10, -12) menu:Show() end UIMenu_StopCounting(menu) else UIMenu_StopCounting(this:GetParent()) end end
function UIMenuButton_OnLeave() UIMenu_StartCounting(this:GetParent()) if this.nested then UIMenu_StartCounting(getglobal(this.nested)) end end

Labels/shortcuts quoted from GlobalStrings. Language (benilla has no language -- model yet) and Macro (no macro frame) are deliberately out; this OnLoad is their -- return path. function BenillaChatMenu_Type(prefix) local eb = ChatFrameEditBox eb:Show() eb:SetFocus() eb:SetText(prefix .. (eb:GetText() or "")) end
function ChatMenu_OnLoad() UIMenu_Initialize() UIMenu_AddButton("Say", "/s", function() BenillaChatMenu_Type("/s ") end) UIMenu_AddButton("Party Chat", "/p", function() BenillaChatMenu_Type("/p ") end) UIMenu_AddButton("Guild Chat", "/g", function() BenillaChatMenu_Type("/g ") end) UIMenu_AddButton("Yell", "/y", function() BenillaChatMenu_Type("/y ") end) UIMenu_AddButton("Whisper", "/w", function() BenillaChatMenu_Type("/w ") end) UIMenu_AddButton("Emote", "/e", function() BenillaChatMenu_Type("/e ") end, "EmoteMenu") UIMenu_AddButton("Reply", "/r", function() BenillaChatMenu_Type("/r ") end) UIMenu_AddButton("Voice Emote", nil, nil, "VoiceMacroMenu") end
